seo.title: Search Console Manual Actions: How to Fix
seo.meta_description: What a Search Console manual action is, how to find affected pages, fix them and request review, explained for Anaheim and Orange County business websites.

h1: Search Console Manual Actions: What They Are and How to Fix Them
answer: Search Console manual actions are issued when a human reviewer at Google decides pages on a site don't comply with Google's spam policies. Affected pages can rank lower or be removed from results. The Manual actions report shows any actions, which pages are affected and how to request review once everything is fixed. Anaheim and Orange County businesses should check it regularly.
key_takeaways: Issued by human reviewers at Google.
Pages can rank lower or be omitted.
Fix every affected page, not some.
Then request review with a clear explanation.
Reviews take several days or weeks.

sections.heading: What a manual action is
sections.body_html: Google's help page says it issues a manual action when a human reviewer determines that pages on a site aren't compliant with Google's spam policies. Most manual actions address attempts to manipulate Google's search index.

sections.heading: What happens to the site
sections.body_html: Google says most issues lead to pages or sites being ranked lower or omitted from search results, without any visual indication to searchers. Some or all of the site may be affected.

sections.heading: How you'll know
sections.body_html: Google notifies you in the Manual actions report and in the Search Console message center. The report shows a count of manual actions at the top; no actions means a green check mark.

sections.heading: Which pages are affected
sections.body_html: Expand the action description to see patterns of affected pages. It might be a directory, such as /real-estate/*, or Affects all pages for site-wide actions. Not every page matching a pattern is necessarily affected.

sections.heading: How to fix
sections.body_html:
1. Expand the description and follow the Learn more link for that type of action.
  2. Fix the issue on all affected pages; fixing some won't earn a partial return.
  3. If there are several actions, fix all of them.
  4. Make sure Google can reach the pages: no login, paywall, robots.txt block or noindex.
  5. Select Request Review and describe your fixes.

sections.heading: A good reconsideration request
sections.body_html: Google says a good request explains the exact quality issue, describes the steps you took to fix it and documents the outcome. Be specific and honest; vague requests slow the process.

sections.heading: How long it takes
sections.body_html: Google says most reconsideration reviews take several days or weeks, and some, such as link-related requests, can take longer. You'll be told of progress by email.

sections.heading: Bought a site?
sections.body_html: If you bought a site that broke the policies before you owned it, Google says to fix the issues and mention in your request that you recently acquired the site and that it now complies.

sections.heading: How to avoid manual actions
sections.body_html:
• Don't buy or sell links meant to manipulate rankings.
  • Don't publish scaled, low-value pages made only for search.
  • Don't hide text or show different content to Google.
  • Keep user-generated areas, such as comments, free of spam.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Fixing a sample of pages and requesting review.
  • Submitting a request without explaining what changed.
  • Blocking affected pages so Google can't verify fixes.
  • Ignoring Search Console messages.
  • Assuming a traffic drop is a manual action without checking the report.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether a ranking drop means a manual action. Usually not; most drops come from competition, seasonality or algorithm updates, and the report will show a green check mark if there's no action. Another question is whether an agency's past work can cause one. Yes, for example paid link schemes; fix them and explain in your request. Owners also ask whether to start a new domain instead. Google recommends fixing the problem and filing a reconsideration request.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• Manual actions report checked.
  • Search Console messages read.
  • All affected pages fixed.
  • Pages reachable by Google.
  • Clear reconsideration request sent.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a law firm in Newport Beach that hired a cheap SEO provider years ago, who bought links on unrelated sites. The firm finds an unnatural links manual action. It documents the paid links, asks site owners to remove them, disavows the rest, and sends a reconsideration request listing the steps and outcome. After several weeks, the action is lifted.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: This task is one piece of a wider local plan. Google says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity, so the profile, your website and your reputation all have to agree. A practical order for most Orange County businesses is: get the Business Profile verified and accurate, make the name, address and phone identical everywhere, publish one clear page per service, then build a steady habit of genuine reviews and replies. Each step makes the next one work better, and the same signals help AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI features describe your business correctly when someone in Anaheim asks for a recommendation.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Open the Manual actions report.
  2. Check Search Console messages.
  3. Review any past SEO work for risky tactics.
  4. Note who will act if an action appears.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: Most of this can be done in-house with an hour or two and careful reading of Google's own help pages. It is worth bringing in help when the stakes are high or the problem keeps coming back: a profile that has been suspended more than once, many locations to manage, a site that keeps failing the same checks, or no time to keep up the routine. A good local SEO partner should explain what they will change and why, point to Google's guidelines rather than promise rankings, and leave you with access to every account. Chimera works this way with businesses across Anaheim and Orange County.

sections.heading: Keeping records that make a review easier
sections.body_html: If you ever need to send a reconsideration request, good records make it faster and more convincing. Keep a simple log of the SEO and marketing work done on your site: who did it, when and what it involved, including any link building, guest posting or content production. Keep copies of agency reports and invoices. If you receive a manual action, add to the log each step you take: the pages or links you found, what you changed or removed, which site owners you contacted and when, and what remains. Google says a good request explains the exact issue, the steps taken and the outcome; a log lets you write that clearly instead of from memory. It also protects the business when people change: a new marketing manager or agency can see what happened before and avoid repeating it. For businesses in Anaheim and across Orange County that have worked with several providers over the years, this record is often the missing piece when a problem surfaces.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Check the Manual actions report monthly. If there's an action, fix every affected page, make them reachable and send a clear reconsideration request. Chimera, based in Anaheim, helps Orange County businesses clean up past SEO problems.

faqs.q: What is a manual action in Search Console?
faqs.a: An action Google takes when a human reviewer finds pages that don't comply with its spam policies.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have one?
faqs.a: The Manual actions report and Search Console messages tell you; no actions shows a green check mark.

faqs.q: Can I fix only some pages?
faqs.a: No. Google says fixing some pages won't earn a partial return.
Google says several days or weeks, sometimes longer for link issues.

faqs.q: What should a reconsideration request include?
faqs.a: The exact issue, the steps taken to fix it and the outcome.

faqs.q: I bought the site; what do I do?
faqs.a: Fix the issues and say in your request that you recently acquired the site.

faqs.q: Do you help businesses in Anaheim and Orange County with this?
faqs.a: Yes. Chimera is based in Anaheim, California and works with businesses across Orange County, California.
